rules.rule: Calendar Sky aspect copy never uses you, your, yours, yourself, or yourselves; Sky placement copy may address the reader directly.
rules.rationale: Calendar Sky aspects describe collective events, while Sky placement pages may speak directly to the reader under the owner-approved page register.
examplesAllowed: The aspect changes what the group can agree to.

mechanical.message: Calendar Sky aspect copy is collective; second person belongs to Sky placement, natal, or transit-to-natal copy.

rules.rule: Do not use em dashes.
rules.rationale: Standing owner punctuation rule.
examplesAllowed: The plan changes because someone finally says no.
examplesRejected: The plan changes—someone finally says no.

mechanical.message: Em dashes are not used in reader copy.

rules.rule: Do not use people in Sky Placement. On other surfaces, use it only when the collective itself is the real subject and a more exact subject would be less accurate.
rules.rationale: Generic people repeatedly conceals the actual subject in Sky Placement while remaining legitimate in some collective contexts.
examplesAllowed: A sibling stops hosting every holiday.
examplesRejected: People can care deeply and still leave the rule untouched.

mechanical.message: Name the group, role, action, message, or decision instead of generic people.

rules.rule: Person is allowed. Prohibit repetitive generic phrases such as one person when a more specific role, action, or subject is available.
rules.rationale: The word is natural in owner writing; repetition becomes formulaic and can hide who acts.
examplesAllowed: The person who remembers every birthday keeps the spare key.
examplesRejected: One person decides. One person explains. One person fixes it.

mechanical.message: Repeated generic one person phrasing must name the role, action, or actual subject.

rules.rule: Looks good on paper is allowed as an ordinary idiom. Other uses of on paper require an actual written document; administrative put the plan on paper phrasing is prohibited.
rules.rationale: The owner uses the ordinary idiom but rejected AI-generated administrative instructions.
examplesAllowed: It looks good on paper.
The signed contract exists on paper.
examplesRejected: Put the emergency plan on paper.

mechanical.message: Use on paper only for the ordinary looks-good-on-paper idiom or when a physical written document matters.

rules.rule: Room is allowed for a literal physical room. Prohibit stock audience or hierarchy phrases such as the loudest person in the room or the smartest voice in the room.
rules.rationale: Literal rooms provide useful evidence; room-as-audience phrasing is a stock hierarchy cliché.
examplesAllowed: A guest room turns into an office.
examplesRejected: The loudest person in the room becomes the plan.
The smartest voice in the room takes over.

mechanical.message: Name who takes over and what everyone else does instead of using a stock room-as-hierarchy phrase.

rules.rule: Steady is allowed for observable effort, pace, support, light, or reliability. Prohibit it only as vague energy language or an empty positive adjective.
rules.rationale: Published owner writing uses steady naturally; the earlier stable, strong, or solid qualifier rule did not evaluate the noun or sentence.
examplesAllowed: A full day in Taurus emphasizes steady effort.
The support remains steady.

mechanical.message: Use steady for something observable, not as vague energy language.

rules.rule: Perform, performed, and performance are allowed only for literal acting, music, presentations, or measurable job performance. Prohibit figurative uses about identity, normalcy, worth, emotion, belonging, or social behavior; Leo alone is not an exception.
rules.rationale: The words are ordinary in literal performance contexts but repeatedly became polished figurative framing in generated copy.
examplesAllowed: The actor prepares for the performance.
The manager reviews quarterly job performance.
examplesRejected: Life is not a performance review.

mechanical.message: Use the performance family only for literal acting, music, presentations, or measurable job performance.

literal_exceptions: an actual physical object is tilted

rules.rule: Do not use tilt or tilts as a figurative substitute for change. Literal physical tilting is allowed.
rules.rationale: The owner rejected tilt in this phrasing and explicitly retained the physical-object exception.
examplesAllowed: The table tilts toward the window.
examplesRejected: A dinner plan starts to tilt.

mechanical.message: Use the verb only for a physically tilted object; name the actual change otherwise.

rules.rule: A tagline must be a clear full sentence readers understand on first read. Strong is welcome; cryptic compression is not.
rules.rationale: The owner retired Stop calling silence peace because the compressed line did not make sense without explanation.
examplesAllowed: The disagreement starts before the cancellation.

mechanical.message: The tagline must be a clear full sentence rather than a compressed slogan.

rules.rule: Do not turn ordinary events into institutional, advocacy, therapy-workbook, or corporate-operations language unless the actual subject requires it.
rules.rationale: These registers repeatedly replace recognizable behavior with categories and reports.
examplesAllowed: Everyone else has to change their plans later.
examplesRejected: Document the task and record what fails.

mechanical.message: Use ordinary language and name the action instead of an institutional or operations label.

literal_exceptions: physical mail is part of the source or scene

rules.rule: Use message, reply, response, or what they were told instead of letter or formal technical delivery terms unless physical mail matters.
rules.rationale: Letter sounded dated, while portal notification and electronic correspondence sounded technical rather than current.
examplesAllowed: Three families compare the messages they received.
A handwritten letter arrives in the mail.
examplesRejected: Three families receive the same portal notification.

mechanical.message: Default to message, reply, or response unless physical mail matters.

rules.rule: Chani-adjacent warmth, tenderness, permission, emotional intelligence, and moderate lyrical cadence are allowed. Documented adjacent-site constructions and advocacy-default subject matter are not.
rules.rationale: Softness is not the problem; recognizable borrowed constructions and the wrong recurring subject matter are.
examplesAllowed: Warm, emotionally observant permission to do one nameable thing.
examplesRejected: Let's dive into what the stars have in store.

terms: Let's dive into what the stars have in store
mechanical.message: This exact adjacent-site construction is not house voice.

rules.rule: Reject the swappable tagline construction [Planet] in [sign] helps us grow through [generic virtue or domain]. A tagline must tell the reader what is actually happening.
rules.rationale: Naming a placement and generic virtue produces interchangeable astrology copy rather than a recognizable line.
examplesAllowed: The plan changes when someone finally says what they want.
examplesRejected: Jupiter in Libra helps us grow through fair, honest partnership.

mechanical.pattern: \b(?:Sun|Moon|Mercury|Venus|Mars|Jupiter|Saturn|Uranus|Neptune|Pluto|Chiron|Lilith|North Node|South Node) in (?:Aries|Taurus|Gemini|Cancer|Leo|Virgo|Libra|Scorpio|Sagittarius|Capricorn|Aquarius|Pisces) helps us (?:grow|learn|heal|change|connect) through\b
mechanical.message: The tagline is a swappable planet-sign virtue summary rather than a recognizable event.

rules.rule: Reject the stock gift-to-problem keyword flip: The gift becomes the problem when [positive keyword] turns into [negative keyword]. Show the observed sequence instead.
rules.rationale: The formula reads like a generic astrology gift-and-shadow template.
examplesAllowed: The cancellation is where the disagreement finally shows up.
examplesRejected: The gift becomes the problem when diplomacy turns into avoidance.

mechanical.message: Name the observed pressure, behavior, and cost instead of flipping a gift keyword into a shadow keyword.

rules.rule: Reject generic fairness conclusions that explain a virtue instead of ending on the specific behavior and cost established by the article.
rules.rationale: The controlled article ended with a universal principle that could close many unrelated relationship articles.
examplesAllowed: After enough of this, no one trusts what is said anymore.
examplesRejected: Fairness requires each side to be heard before the choice is made.

mechanical.message: End on the article's specific behavior and cost, not a universal fairness principle.

rules.rule: Reject sign-cliche stock scenes when they govern the central opening, tension, and development sequence. Isolated practical moves are exempt unless the central scene itself is a scheduling or dinner scene. The scene must follow from this placement's combined meaning at this transit's scale, and a year-long or slower transit cannot be reduced to one evening's logistics.
rules.rationale: The rejected Jupiter-in-Libra draft passed the earlier checks while reproducing the named Libra dinner-plan meme and shrinking a year-long transit to one evening.
examplesAllowed: A sequence whose pressure and consequence could only follow from the combined planet and sign meaning at the stated duration.
A creative-collaboration article may include separate moves about answering an invitation and naming which day works; those moves do not turn the central scene into invitation scheduling.
examplesRejected: Libra friends cannot choose a restaurant or dinner plan.
Aries goes to the gym or gets an impulsive haircut.
Cancer takes a bubble bath or cancels plans.

mechanical.message: This is a stock sign scene rather than a placement-specific sequence at the transit's scale.

rules.rule: Moves must sound like actions someone would actually say they took, not workshop, facilitation, negotiation, or project-management instructions. Until an exact owner-approved moves exemplar exists, the moves section is the highest-risk section and any listed facilitation term there is a score-1 failure.
rules.rationale: The owner corpus does not yet supply an approved bulleted-moves exemplar, and the rejected draft invented facilitation-workshop language.
examplesAllowed: An ordinary action stated in words someone would use after doing it.

mechanical.message: Moves use facilitation or project-management language instead of an ordinary action.

rules.rule: A qualitative, non-numeric subperiod may trace to a reviewed residency fact only when it cannot exceed that residency. Numeric or date-like subperiods still require an explicit engine fact or render token.
rules.rationale: Narrative pacing inside a known residency window is not a new moving fact, but numeric and calendar-like claims must remain engine-owned.
examplesAllowed: A few months in
Early in the transit
By midyear

mechanical.message: Qualitative subperiods must fit a reviewed residency; numeric or date-like subperiods require an engine fact.

rules.rule: Do not use leak, leaks, leaked, or leaking in Marie Satori editorial copy. Name the observable action or consequence instead.
rules.rationale: The house style guide already prohibited leak language for emotion or expression, and the owner confirmed that leak is an AI tell she does not use.
examplesAllowed: After enough of this, no one trusts what is said anymore.
examplesRejected: Say the raw thing and it clears. Hold it in and it leaks out sideways, aimed at whoever is closest.

mechanical.message: Leak language is an AI tell in Marie Satori copy; name what someone does and what happens because of it.

rules.rule: Keep the architecture fixed: verified astrology supplies meaning, Sol writes one draft, deterministic checks catch hard failures, Terra judges afterward, and only the owner approves exact wording.
rules.rationale: Durable corrections should update scoped policy and regression tests rather than trigger another architecture redesign.

rules.rule: Display time in the user's local timezone; computed dates, degrees, motion, and event times come from the engine rather than generated prose.
rules.rationale: Reader output must not hardcode PT or hand-write moving facts.
examplesRejected: All event times are shown in PT.

rules.rule: Use 17 arcminutes as the primary traditional cazimi figure; a claim of within 1 degree must be flaggable.
rules.rationale: The reference fact bank distinguishes the primary traditional figure from broader modern usage.
examplesAllowed: Cazimi is within 17 arcminutes under the primary traditional figure.

rules.rule: The Barbault quote remains unverified and cannot serve until independently confirmed.
rules.rationale: Unverified quotations cannot become factual authority.
